why: The copy draws a bold w-form at the start of line 13, in sign ink, not a thin printed label.
The copy's i-form, cross-bar and tall stroke make one b+i ligature like the type's joined 4ν, so there is no third sign.
The printed 3 joined to i has a pointed middle and a long descender to the lower left, the type's ẖ, not the closed s.
The hatched sign between w and s is a slash crossed by hatching, so o with doubt.
The hatched long-tailed sign could be n or k; no entry covers it. The 9-shaped sign after it is e, and the next sign is b (see notes).
The v-shaped sign before the divider is b, as both readings have; my ḫ there was an alignment of a different sign.
The c-shaped ḫ and the 3 (s) are clear; the last small 5-form could be e or l.
The heavy looped sign before the final i of line 3 is w, not a second i.
The 2-shaped sign with a long tail and the small 5-form before it make one a; there is no separate e and p.
The 5-form and the long-tailed 2 together are a, as in the a-signs of Kar. 42.
After o s the copy shows a v-shaped b and a separate short slash (o), not one n.
